name: 5 squares in the smallest square
description: The smallest square containing 5 unit squares, read directly: the shapes are placed freely and the container is what the engine measures around them. The optimum is 2 + sqrt(2)/2 = 2.70710678118654, proved by Frits Gobel in 1979 (Friedman's packing pages), and it is a rigid packing: four squares in the corners and one turned 45 degrees in the middle. The direct reading scores 1/side, which is the common scale the same instance scores read the other way round on a unit arena. The solution loaded by default is Goebel's rigid packing: four squares in the corners and one turned 45 degrees, whose side is 2 + sqrt(2)/2 exactly.
